about_the_game:
There’s no escape. No guidance. Just the wind through dead branches… and something moving in the fog.

Everstill Valley is a slow-burning, lo-fi survival horror experience set in a decaying, dreamlike wilderness. Scavenge what you can. Manage your hunger and sanity. And always keep an eye on the trees - something is out there, and it doesn’t stop.

Explore unsettling locations that feel misplaced: a phone booth deep in the forest. A metro tunnel that goes nowhere. A mountain-sized husk kneeling to the sky. Nothing makes sense here - and the longer you stay, the harder it becomes to trust your own thoughts.

About the Demo

This demo offers a first glimpse into the world of Everstill Valley, showcasing the core survival mechanics, atmosphere, and sense of quiet dread.

In this demo, you’ll experience:

  • A sizeable portion of the open world game, including the abandoned house, swamp, and surrounding woods

  • Full day/night cycle with dynamic fog and lighting

  • Survival systems: manage hunger, health, and sanity

  • Encounter the stalker, a slow, unrelenting presence after dark

  • Discover hidden paths, environmental secrets, and cryptic notes left behind by the ones who came before

  • Basic crafting and resource gathering

  • Lo-fi PSX-inspired visuals and minimalist UI focused on immersion

Full Game Will Include

  • A world nearly three times larger, with more to uncover, lose, or survive in

  • Expanded crafting system, resource management, and character upgrades

  • Deeper exploration, with new regions, mysteries, and strange environmental storytelling

  • More lore, more tools, more choices - and more ways to lose your mind

  • A sandbox structure: no clear ending… unless you invent one

Developer Note

This project is still evolving.

If you try the demo, I’d love your thoughts - on anything from mechanics to mood. Your feedback will help shape the final experience. Strange as this world is, it needs explorers.

No combat. No hand-holding. Just you, the dark, and your choices.

How long can you survive when even your thoughts begin to turn on you?
